title: Edit-refusal test asserts the full absolute temp path, which the 180-char display bound can cut on a deeper temp root
outcome: an_edit_refusal_names_the_file_the_tool_reported (src/tests/engram_carried_checks.rs) asserts that the refusal contains the whole absolute target <test temp root>/engram-turn-check-carried-edit-named-project/target/probe.py. engram_display_reported_target cuts the middle of any escaped target over 180 chars (60 head + 120 tail). Here the path is about 155 chars, so the test passes only because the user's temp root is short. A longer temp root (another user name, or another TEMP location) makes it fail for a reason unrelated to the product. The test asserts something independent of where the machine's temp folder is: the displayed form computed through engram_display_reported_target, or the label plus the stable "target/probe.py" tail. It still covers an outside-the-worktree target that fences the gate.
acceptance: an_edit_refusal_names_the_file_the_tool_reported no longer depends on the length of the test temp root: it asserts the displayed target (or a stable suffix and the tool-reported label) and still reports an edit outside the worktree that fences the gate.
The test passes with a target path longer than 180 chars as well as a short one.
